name: Café con leche
caffeine: From the espresso or strong coffee, roughly half the cup; the milk adds none.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will make a café con leche, and at what price.

what: Spanish for coffee with milk: strong coffee, usually espresso, with about an equal measure of milk heated rather than textured, carrying little or no foam. It takes espresso like a latte and the equal measure of a café au lait. Without a machine it is made with strong dark brewed coffee.
taste: Round, milky and mellow, more coffee than a latte, smooth rather than airy since the milk carries so little foam.

steps: Pull a double, 18 to 20 g in, 36 to 40 g out, or brew strong dark roast.
Heat about an equal measure of milk, adding little air and spinning it smooth, without a cap of foam.
Cut the steam near 135 to 140F (57 to 60C); it serves at 140 to 150F (60 to 66C).
Pour it into the coffee in a warmed cup, stir once, and offer sugar.
make.ratio: About equal parts coffee and hot milk
make.dose: 18 to 20 g coffee; milk about equal
make.cup: Warmed 4 to 8 oz cup on a saucer

serve: On a saucer with a teaspoon and sugar on the side. It suits breakfast, and the guest who wants a milky coffee without a latte's foam.
story: Café con leche is the Spanish-speaking world's coffee with milk, and the name is the whole recipe: espresso where there is a machine, strong brewed coffee where there is not, the milk heated in a pan or steamed. A guest who orders it by name knows how they like it, so ask.
guest: Strong coffee with about an equal measure of hot milk and almost no foam: smoother than espresso, more coffee forward than a latte.
watch: Built tall with a foam cap it becomes a latte; keep the milk smooth and the measure near equal.
Ask how the guest takes it: espresso or brewed, stronger or milkier, sweet or not.
Past 160F (71C) the milk tastes cooked and loses its sweetness.

recall.prompt: How is a café con leche made?
recall.answer: A double espresso or strong dark brewed coffee in a warmed cup, with about an equal measure of milk heated to 140 to 150F (60 to 66C), smooth and nearly foamless. Round and milky.

quiz.q: What sets a café con leche apart from a latte?
options: Cold milk poured over a ristretto
quiz.explain: It runs close to half coffee, half milk, heated rather than textured; a latte carries far more milk and a foam layer.

quiz.q: Translated from Spanish, café con leche means what?
quiz.explain: Con leche means with milk. Stained milk is the latte macchiato; cut coffee is the cortado.

quiz.q: With no espresso machine, what is café con leche made from?
quiz.explain: Strong dark brewed coffee and hot milk in about equal parts. Chicory belongs to the New Orleans café au lait, not to this drink.
